sections.h2: St. Johns County housing market in brief
sections.html:
St. Johns grew from 190,039 people in 2010 to 273,425 in 2020 and an estimated 346,328 by mid-2025. Owners occupy 82.2 percent of the 115,794 households, and the midpoint owner home is valued at $489,200. Permits reached 4,735 in 2025, so a seller competes with plenty of new construction.

Owners with a mortgage report a median monthly cost of $2,351, against $728 for those without one. For a newer buyer, much of the carrying cost is the loan and not the tax, which is worth remembering when you talk about the bill.

sections.h2: Help for new owners from the property appraiser
sections.html:
The appraiser's new owner page gives buyers a short checklist: find the parcel's record card, complete the sales questionnaire, and verify the name and mailing address, because the TRIM notice and bill go to that address. A button on the record card estimates the tax bill.

  • Customer service: 904-827-5500.
  • Business equipment returns: 904-827-5508.
  • Building department: 904-827-6800.
  • Planning and zoning: 904-209-0675.
  • Utility department: 904-209-2700.

Owners also update a Florida driver license through the tax collector, a step that matters because the homestead application checks that the license shows the homestead address. New business owners may need a local business tax application and an account with the appraiser.

sections.h2: Key dates in the tax year
sections.html:
• January 1: the property's status sets its value for the assessment year, and ownership and residence on this day decide homestead eligibility.
  • January 1 to April 1: business equipment returns are filed.
  • March 1: filing closes for homestead, other personal exemptions, classified use, agricultural classification and organizational exemptions.
  • August and September: TRIM notices go out with proposed assessments, millage and hearing dates.
  • November: the tax collector mails bills.

When March 1 lands on a weekend, the cutoff moves to the next business day.

For the 2026 tax year the exemption is $51,411, now indexed to inflation. A first block of $25,000 applies to every levy, school bills included. The remaining $26,411 applies to assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000 and leaves school tax untouched.

To qualify, you must be a Florida permanent resident who holds title and lives in the home on January 1. Neither spouse may claim a residency-based exemption in another state, and the office wants proof. Applicants bring a Florida license or ID showing the homestead address and Social Security numbers for both spouses, which are required for online filing. A noncitizen needs a Permanent Resident Card. If you owned a Florida home before, give its address or parcel number. If you close after January 1, that year's exemption is out of reach for the new owner's own claim, so the buyer files the following year.

Once approved, you need not reapply unless marital status, ownership or title changes. A late application for just cause can be filed through the end of the TRIM period, which usually falls late in August.

sections.h2: Renting a homestead, trusts and LLCs
sections.html:
Renting part of a home is fine. The portion you do not rent stays eligible, and a garage apartment or other separate rental space can be carved out while the rest keeps the exemption. Renting the whole property for more than 30 days in two consecutive tax years ends the exemption, and a rental lasting over six months in a tax year is presumed commercial.

Ownership structure matters too. Property held in a trust qualifies if the applicant is the trustee or the trust language gives beneficial title. Moving the house into an LLC or another business entity counts as a change of ownership, which strips every exemption and cap. After a divorce or marriage, the appraiser may ask for a new application, and it sends notice when the deed is recorded in St. Johns County. If the deed is recorded elsewhere, you are responsible for telling the office.

sections.h2: Portability of your Save Our Homes benefit
sections.html:
Portability lets you carry the gap between market and assessed value, up to $500,000, from one Florida homestead to another. The move must happen within three tax years, counted January through December from the sale, and a December sale counts as one tax year.

Downsizing is allowed, and the transferable amount shrinks in proportion to the lower value of the new home. Everyone who owned the old home and owns the new one must apply together, and each spouse of a married couple counts. You can use portability any number of times but never from outside Florida. Spouses who abandon a jointly titled home may split the difference with Form DR-501TS, provided they were married on the abandonment date. The benefit total appears on the TRIM notice and the record card. Non-homestead property carries a separate 10 percent cap, and that benefit cannot be ported.

sections.h2: Other exemptions and the proof they need
sections.html:
All of these are due by March 1, and the office asks applicants to visit in person.

Selected personal exemptions
ExemptionAmountProof asked for
Age 65 or older, limited incomeUp to $50,000Form DR-501SC and prior year household income
Widowed$5,000Mark it on the homestead form or give the death certificate
Blind$5,000Form DR-416 or DR-416B, or SSDI proof
Totally and permanently disabled civilian$5,000Form DR-416 or SSDI letter
Veteran disabled 10 percent or more$5,000DD-214 and a VA disability letter
Combat-related disabled veteran, 65 or olderEqual to the disability ratingForm DR-501DV, DD-214, VA letter

The appraiser also lists total exemptions for quadriplegics, for certain permanent disabilities with limited income, for those totally and permanently disabled through service, for surviving spouses of those who died on active duty and for first responders disabled in the line of duty, plus a deployment exemption on Form DR-501M. Churches, schools, hospitals, nursing homes, affordable housing and historic buildings fall under property-use exemptions. With 22.5 percent of residents 65 or older, many sellers qualify for something here.

Start with a conversation at the appraiser's office. If that fails, a petition goes to the Value Adjustment Board. The TRIM notice goes out in mid-August, and you may file within 25 days of that mailing. The date is printed at the top of the notice.

The Clerk of the Circuit Court and County Comptroller manages the process and posts the petition form, at 904-819-3600. A denied exemption, classification or portability claim has its own 30 day window, so if you think the assessment is too high, act before you list the house.

sections.h2: Stamp tax, delinquency and closing payoffs
sections.html:
Stamp tax is seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price and binds every party named on the deed. The clerk charges $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each page after it. Debt that stays on the house is counted in the price.

Unpaid bills turn delinquent April 1, certificates are sold by June 1, and a holder may apply for a deed after two years, with half the latest assessed value added to the opening bid on homestead land. Ask the collector for a payoff and have the title company search for certificates.

On a cash sale the same payoffs apply, but there is no lender appraisal or underwriting to wait for, so closing can move as fast as the title work allows. Bring your deed, a recent tax bill and any payoff letters to the title company on day one.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 homestead exemption total in St. Johns County?
faqs.a: $51,411. The first $25,000 reaches all levies and $26,411 applies to value between $50,000 and $75,000, excluding school taxes.

faqs.q: Is the March 1 homestead deadline ever different?
faqs.a: Yes. When March 1 falls on a weekend, filing moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Does a St. Johns County buyer keep the seller's capped value?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets the home to market value the next January 1. The seller may port up to $500,000 of the gap to a new Florida homestead within three tax years.

faqs.q: Can I rent my whole St. Johns County homestead for a few months?
faqs.a: Renting the entire home for more than 30 days in two consecutive tax years ends the exemption. A rental beyond six months in one year is presumed commercial.

faqs.q: Who runs the Value Adjustment Board paperwork?
faqs.a: The circuit clerk and comptroller, at 904-819-3600. A petition is due 25 days after TRIM notices are mailed.
